q: Sherry is chalk-marked twice. Explain both sets of marks — those of the first classification and the palmas of the second — and what each decides.
accept: raya palo cortado slash marks decide fino oloroso track
una raya dos rayas palma cortada
una raya fino dos rayas oloroso tres rayas distillation
ans: Two sets of marks. At the FIRST classification the rayas set the track: una raya (/) clean and delicate → flor/fino track, fortified to ~15%; dos rayas (//) fuller or coarser → oloroso track at 17%+; tres rayas (///) defective → distillation or vinegar; the raya struck through marks the palo cortado anomaly. At the SECOND classification, on wines already under flor, the palmas grade the fino itself: una palma a young, clean fino; dos palmas an older one; tres palmas a fino of six to eight years verging on amontillado; cuatro palmas a wine whose flor has died, in effect an old amontillado. Palma cortada marks a fino turning toward palo cortado.
exp: The capataz's chalk decides the wine's entire life in one stroke.

q: Which Spanish region grows vines in volcanic pits behind crescent walls, and what are they called?
accept: lanzarote geria zocos hoyos
canary islands lanzarote hoyos zocos
ans: Lanzarote (La Geria): vines in hoyos (pits) behind zocos (semicircular stone walls) in black picón ash
exp: Malvasía Volcánica; ungrafted, hand-dug, one of viticulture's great images.

godello treixadura

q: What did the 2017 Rioja reform allow producers to put on labels for the first time in the region's modern era?
accept: vino de zona municipio vinedo singular espumoso
zone village single vineyard and sparkling rioja

accept: multi-vintage blend of three years released as nv
blend of several unico vintages
several unico vintages blended and released as nv
multi-vintage blend of unico
multi-vintage blend of unico released without a vintage
ans: A multi-vintage blend (typically three Único vintages) released without a year — the estate's own solera logic
exp: Valbuena 5° is the earlier-released sibling; Alión and Pintia the family's other estates.

q: Which grape dominates Spanish acreage by hectare, and where?
accept: tempranillo
tempranillo la mancha rioja ribera
tempranillo overtook airen
airen la mancha castilla
airén central plateau
ans: Tempranillo — c. 203,000 ha massed across Castilla-La Mancha, Rioja and Ribera del Duero, ahead of Airén (c. 200,000 ha) since MAPA's survey with data to 31 July 2021. Airén, the vast dry-farmed plateau white of Castilla-La Mancha (much of it distilled to brandy), held the title for decades and remains much the largest white.
exp: Spain has the world's largest vineyard area, and these two varieties are roughly two-fifths of it. Airén led for decades, but MAPA's plantings survey (data to 31 July 2021) put Tempranillo at 202,917 ha against Airén's 200,084 ha — Airén has shed some 138,000 ha since 2000 while Tempranillo has gained about 80,000.

garnacha gredos comando g

exp: Burgundian-toned Garnacha at altitude west of Madrid; the decade's Spanish story.

q: Explain the modern argument between Rioja's aging tiers and its terroir movement.
accept: crianza reserva time-based versus site-based classification
aging tiers versus single vineyard identity
ans: The classic tiers classify by time in oak; the new movement insists place should classify wine — hence viñedo singular, and Artadi's exit
exp: Time versus place: the same fight Burgundy settled centuries ago.

q: Explain the criaderas y solera system, and why a sherry's average age can exceed the age of any barrel in it.
accept: fractional blending through scales so the average age exceeds any single barrel
solera and criaderas refreshed in sequence by saca and rocio
running wine down through the scales raises the average age indefinitely
nothing is ever emptied so a trace of every vintage remains
ans: The wine is held in scales: the solera on the floor, the criaderas stacked above it in order of increasing youth. Wine for sale is drawn from the solera — the saca, and only a fraction of each butt is taken — that scale is topped up from the first criadera, which is topped up from the second, and so on to the youngest scale, which receives the new vintage, the rocío. Nothing is ever emptied, so every butt retains an exponentially decaying trace of every year that has ever entered it: the mathematical average age climbs indefinitely, while no barrel anywhere in the system holds unblended old wine. That fractional blending has three purposes — it erases vintage variation so the house style is reproducible, it keeps biological wines supplied with the fresh nutrients flor needs to survive, and it lets a small stock of very old wine season a much larger volume. Jerez requires a minimum of two years' ageing.
exp: Two consequences to have ready: flor is a living organism that starves without refreshment, which is the practical reason finos are run so often; and consistency, not age, is the system's original commercial purpose — it was built to satisfy a shipping trade that wanted the same wine every year.

q: Explain what the recent reform of the Jerez DO changed.
accept: the ageing zone was widened unfortified wines allowed and old varieties restored
the triangle was opened up and vino de pasto was legalised
recognised unfortified pasto wines vineyard pago names and historic grapes
brought vineyard identity vintage and old varieties back into the do
ans: It reopened the region to its own history. The ageing zone had been confined to Jerez de la Frontera, El Puerto de Santa María and Sanlúcar — the famous triangle — and was extended across the wider production zone, so towns like Trebujena, Chipiona, Chiclana and Rota that had always grown grapes may now age wine under the DO. Unfortified wines were recognised, which legitimised the vino de pasto movement that had been forced to sell its Palomino as table wine outside the appellation. Single-vineyard pago names and vintage-dated wines may now be labelled. And historic varieties beyond Palomino, Pedro Ximénez and Moscatel — among them Beba, Perruno, Vejeriego, Cañocazo and the Mantúos — were restored to the permitted list. Taken together it converts a set of rules describing a 20th-century shipping business into rules describing a place.
exp: The trade-off is real: the DO gives up some brand control — a guarantee that sherry means fortified wine aged in three specific towns — in exchange for terroir language it needs to compete for attention. Equipo Navazos, Luis Pérez and Muchada-Léclapart had already proved the market existed outside the rules.

q: What white wine may Ribera del Duero now make, and from what grape?
accept: albillo mayor whites permitted from the 2019 vintage
white ribera del duero based on albillo mayor at least 75 percent
the local albillo mayor was finally allowed as a white wine
albillo mayor which had been interplanted in the red vineyards
~albillo mayor
ans: White Ribera del Duero has been permitted since the 2019 vintage, based on Albillo Mayor — a local white that had been interplanted among the old red vines for generations and was either co-fermented into the reds or sold outside the DO because it had nowhere legal to go. The rule requires a large majority of Albillo Mayor, at least 75 per cent. It is a thick-skinned, low-acid, textural white that gives weight and orchard fruit rather than freshness, and it is best understood as the DO legalising something its growers already possessed. Rosado had always been allowed; it is white that was the gap.
exp: The wider lesson is how often appellation reform is retrospective: the vines were in the ground, the wine was being made, and the law caught up. Compare Rioja's blanco expansion in 2007 and the Jerez pasto question — the same pattern twice more.

q: Explain how Cava has been restructured, and why leading producers left anyway.
accept: split into cava de guarda and guarda superior with zones and organic rules
nine months for guarda then eighteen thirty and thirty six above with zoning
restructured with tiers and zones but corpinnat and raventos still left
the do raised minimums and mapped zones yet the top estates seceded
ans: Cava is now divided into Cava de Guarda, with a minimum of nine months on the lees, and Cava de Guarda Superior, which covers Reserva at eighteen months, Gran Reserva at thirty and Cava de Paraje Calificado at thirty-six. Guarda Superior additionally requires vines of at least ten years, full traceability from a registered plot, and organic certification from the 2025 harvest. The DO has also been mapped into zones and subzones — Comtats de Barcelona, Valle del Ebro, Viñedos de Almendralejo and the Levante — to answer the standing criticism that Cava was a production method scattered across Spain rather than a place. It has not stopped the secessions. Raventós i Blanc left first for its own Conca del Riu Anoia, and Gramona, Recaredo, Torelló and others founded Corpinnat, arguing that raising the floor is no use to producers who need a ceiling that excludes industrial volume.
exp: State the structural point: a denomination whose members range from a co-operative selling at three euros to an estate selling at forty cannot legislate exclusivity, because every rule must be one the majority can meet. That is why prestige tiers inside big DOs so often fail to hold their best producers.

q: Make the case for Montilla-Moriles as something more than a cheaper Jerez.
accept: pedro ximenez based unfortified generosos aged in tinajas in cordoba
px ripens to fifteen percent so fortification is unnecessary
inland cordoba making unfortified finos and the greatest px
same solera system but px instead of palomino and no fortification
ans: It lies inland in Córdoba, hotter and far more continental than the coast, with albariza in its best sites — the Sierra de Montilla and Moriles Alto. Its grape is Pedro Ximénez, not Palomino, and it ripens to such sugar that the base wines reach around fifteen per cent alcohol naturally, so its generosos — fino, amontillado, oloroso — are traditionally made with no fortification at all, which is legally impossible in Jerez. It ferments in tinajas, the tall earthenware jars, it runs the same criaderas y solera system, and it makes the greatest Pedro Ximénez in Spain, having supplied Jerez with sweetening wine for generations. What it lacks is the Atlantic: without Sanlúcar's humidity and cool the flor grows thinner, so the finos are broader, nuttier and shorter-lived under flor than a manzanilla.
exp: The unfortified generoso is the real point of difference and the easiest sell on a list: a fino that never saw spirit. Know also that the historic export of Montilla PX into Jerez has been progressively closed off, which is part of why the region now argues its own case.

q: Recite the pressure classes: Champagne full, pétillant, and the Italian frizzante line.

five to six full one to two half petillant
